<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="שבט_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917075_theRebbe_40" batchId="meluket-_D7_A9_D7_91_D7_98_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917075_theRebbe_40__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the verse's comparison of wisdom to folly, like light's advantage over darkness, teaches that refining external wisdom creates an advantage in Torah wisdom beyond its inherent nature, and Yitro's acknowledgment even elevated the giving of the Torah itself.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it is necessary to understand,</t>
    <t s="1">that from the language of the verse</t>
    <t s="2">(that there is an advantage to wisdom over folly, as the advantage of light over darkness)</t>
    <t s="3">it is implied,</t>
    <t s="4">that this—that the advantage of light is from darkness</t>
    <t s="5">(that through darkness being transformed into light, an advantage is created in the light)—</t>
    <t s="6">is a known thing,</t>
    <t s="7">and the verse innovates</t>
    <t s="8">that likewise it is with wisdom and folly,</t>
    <t s="9">that through the refinement of the wisdom of the side of impurity, an advantage is created in the wisdom of holiness.</t>
    <t s="10">And explanation is needed,</t>
    <t s="11">for ostensibly,</t>
    <t s="12">after one already knows that through the refinement of the side of impurity</t>
    <t s="13">(darkness)</t>
    <t s="14">an advantage is created in holiness</t>
    <t s="15">(light),</t>
    <t s="16">what is the innovation in this—that there is an advantage to wisdom over folly,</t>
    <t s="17">to the point that it says about this "And I saw"</t>
    <t s="18">(King Solomon,</t>
    <t s="19">the wisest of all men).</t>
    <t s="20">And according to the above, it can be said,</t>
    <t s="21">that this—that through darkness being transformed into light an advantage is created in the light—applies to the light that comes and is drawn down through service,</t>
    <t s="22">regarding which it is possible to say that the service of transforming darkness into light draws down a loftier flow than the flow drawn through service in matters of holiness.</t>
    <t s="23">And the innovation of Solomon</t>
    <t s="24">("And I saw")</t>
    <t s="25">is,</t>
    <t s="26">that through the refinement and transformation of the side of impurity into holiness, an advantage is also created in the wisdom of the Torah.</t>
    <t s="27">For although the drawing down and descent of the Torah below is a drawing down from its own essence,</t>
    <t s="28">from the aspect of Above</t>
    <t s="29">[as per the expression "the giving of the Torah,"</t>
    <t s="30">a gift from Above,</t>
    <t s="31">not from the aspect of man's service],</t>
    <t s="32">and also that which a worthy student will innovate through his toil in Torah study was already given to Moshe at Sinai</t>
    <t s="33">(and his toil is to reveal</t>
    <t s="34">that which was already given as a gift,</t>
    <t s="35">a drawing down from Above),</t>
    <t s="36">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="37">through the refinement of the folly of external wisdoms and its transformation into wisdom of holiness</t>
    <t s="38">[when one studies this wisdom</t>
    <t s="39">in order to thereby add knowledge in matters of Torah,</t>
    <t s="40">through which this wisdom is refined and included in the Torah],</t>
    <t s="41">an advantage is created in the wisdom of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="42">higher than it is from its own essence.</t>
    <t s="43">And moreover,</t>
    <t s="44">that through Yitro's acknowledgment</t>
    <t s="45">(before the giving of the Torah)</t>
    <t s="46">an advantage was also created in the entire matter of the giving of the Torah.</t>
    <t s="47">For although the giving of the Torah was in the manner of a drawing down from Above</t>
    <t s="48">[the matters in the Torah that are innovated by the worthy student in each generation,</t>
    <t s="49">although the matters themselves were already given at Sinai,</t>
    <t s="50">their drawing down from concealment to revelation is through the service and toil of the worthy student,</t>
    <t s="51">unlike the drawing down of the giving of the Torah, which was in the manner of a drawing down from Above,</t>
    <t s="52">not through service and toil],</t>
    <t s="53">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="54">through the refinement and transformation of the wisdom of the side of impurity into wisdom of holiness, which occurred through Yitro's acknowledgment,</t>
    <t s="55">an advantage was created</t>
    <t s="56">(as it were)</t>
    <t s="57">also in the Torah that was given at the giving of the Torah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the advantage created in the Torah through Yitro's acknowledgment is that it drew into the Torah the Essence beyond the categories of above and below, thereby enabling innovation through toil and refinement of external wisdoms.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="1">that the advantage</t>
    <t s="2">(as it were)</t>
    <t s="3">that was created in the Torah through Yitro's acknowledgment is,</t>
    <t s="4">that the Torah from its own essence, its matter is a drawing down from Above,</t>
    <t s="5">that the service of the lower realm does not reach there,</t>
    <t s="6">and certainly the service of transforming the darkness of the side of impurity into holiness does not reach there, for regarding the light of the Torah there is no</t>
    <t s="7">(initially)</t>
    <t s="8">darkness,</t>
    <t s="9">and through this—that the giving of the Torah was through Yitro's acknowledgment—</t>
    <t s="10">there was drawn into it the Essence that is beyond the category of above and below,</t>
    <t s="11">light and darkness,</t>
    <t s="12">and through this it was innovated,</t>
    <t s="13">that through service and toil one can innovate in the Torah,</t>
    <t s="14">to expound it,</t>
    <t s="15">and that through the refinement of the folly of external wisdoms there will be an advantage in the wisdom of the Torah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains Yitro's acknowledgment that "G-d is greater than all the gods" in a deeper sense, showing that recognizing the loftiest intermediaries as mere tools of G-d is the ultimate rejection of idolatry.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">D)</t>
    <t s="1">And the explanation of the matter</t>
    <t s="2">(of the advantage created through Yitro acknowledging that "G-d is greater than all the gods")</t>
    <t s="3">in greater depth,</t>
    <t s="4">will be understood by prefacing that ostensibly it is not understood,</t>
    <t s="5">that according to its simple meaning that the intent of "all the gods" is idolatry,</t>
    <t s="6">as Rashi explains on the verse "from all the gods"—it teaches that he was familiar with every idolatry in the world,</t>
    <t s="7">what is the superiority in this that he acknowledged that G-d is greater than all the gods?</t>
    <t s="8">And the explanation can be said according to what the Rambam wrote</t>
    <t s="9">that the beginning of the matter of idolatry is what they thought, that since the Holy One, blessed be He, created the stars and spheres to govern the world and they serve before Him, therefore it is fitting to honor them</t>
    <t s="10">[and their error was in this, that they thought that the stars have dominion to influence by their own choice,</t>
    <t s="11">and they did not know the truth, that He, blessed be He, influences through them as an axe in the hand of the woodcutter].</t>
    <t s="12">And from this it will be understood,</t>
    <t s="13">that the negation of the matter of idolatry applies not only regarding stars and constellations but also regarding all levels of the order of the chain of descent</t>
    <t s="14">(angels,</t>
    <t s="15">Sefiros, etc.)</t>
    <t s="16">through which influence is drawn down below.</t>
    <t s="17">And moreover,</t>
    <t s="18">the more the intermediary is lofty, the more one must negate the error that it is fitting to honor it,</t>
    <t s="19">for it is nothing but an axe in the hand of the woodcutter.</t>
    <t s="20">And as is also understood from what is brought in the Midrash,</t>
    <t s="21">a parable of a king who entered a province and dukes and governors were with him, etc.,</t>
    <t s="22">the greater the minister is,</t>
    <t s="23">and especially the viceroy,</t>
    <t s="24">greater perspicacity is needed to say "I am taking the king."</t>
    <t s="25">And this is that Yitro's acknowledgment that "G-d is greater than all the gods" was dependent on his being familiar with every idolatry in the world,</t>
    <t s="26">for through his having knowledge and recognition of the entire order of the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="27">even to the most lofty level,</t>
    <t s="28">specifically through this</t>
    <t s="29">could he have the knowledge</t>
    <t s="30">("Now I know")</t>
    <t s="31">that "G-d is greater than all the gods."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
